A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same 3DGEER work, with matching authors, algorithms, and benchmark results. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables, and appendices support comparison despite substantial restructuring.

before.justification: V1 reports original ScanNet++, ZipNeRF, and MipNeRF360 experiments, runtime measurements, and PBF/BEAP ablations.

after.justification: V2 retains those empirical results and adds Aria experiments, Gaussian-count scaling, extreme-FoV evaluations, and rendering and numerical-stability analyses.

M1.justification: Both versions use the same canonical ray integral, analytic gradients, PBF-CSF association with mirror handling, BEAP supervision, and training/rendering algorithms. V2's numerical-stability discussion explains the existing cross-product computation rather than introducing a changed core method.

E1.justification: V2 adds two Aria egocentric scenes with moderate-FoV, low-light imagery (Appendix J). It also adds ScanNet++ central-crop-to-full-FoV evaluation and unseen extreme-FoV scenarios, including 170-degree pinhole and 180-degree circular rendering. These materially extend the original datasets and cross-camera tests.

E2.justification: The main benchmark baseline sets largely persist. V2 adds 3DGS to the ScanNet++ comparison and evaluates GOF without filtering against GOF using 3DGEER formulas (Figure C.1); its revised BEAP table drops v1's separate 3DGS comparator. Newly discussed 2DGS and HTGS are conceptual comparisons, not added benchmark evaluations.

E3.justification: New protocols lower FisheyeGS's densification threshold and evaluate 4k–30k checkpoints, replace transmittance separately during inference and training, and expand supervision comparisons across central/full FoV and projection spaces. Gaussian-count, memory, and per-tile workload measurements are added. Table 4 also reverses GPU attribution for unchanged sourced FPS values, without establishing reruns; the original 30k benchmark protocol remains.

E4.justification: V2 adds tests of whether increased Gaussian counts compensate for approximation, train/test-time transmittance substitutions, extreme-FoV robustness, GOF numerical degeneracy, and rendering the same pretrained scene with different engines (Sections 4.1, 4.4 and Appendices C.7, I). BEAP ablations expand substantially. The original PBF cross-association analysis is retained in Table K.6.

E5.justification: V2 Table K.6 newly reports means and standard deviations of Gaussian associations per tile, whereas v1 Table 7 reports only perceptual scores and their differences. This adds descriptive variability reporting, not repeated-run uncertainty. Neither version specifies repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Original benchmark scores and most runtime results are retained, including 31.50 ScanNet++ and 27.76 MipNeRF360 PSNR. Substantial new entries cover Aria, central-crop generalization, scaling, transmittance replacement, memory, and numerical stability. Aria reports average PSNR of 33.5 versus FisheyeGS's 32.8. The original central-only BEAP result set is replaced under an expanded protocol, not shown to improve under identical settings.

T1.justification: The ray-integral theorem, gradient derivations, and PBF solver are retained. V2 adds mathematical reasoning about numerical cancellation for nearly degenerate Gaussians (Appendix C.7, Equation C.14), states a condition for neglecting negative ray parameters (B.2), and identifies perspective-camera equivalences with earlier formulations (D.3). These are limited additions rather than a replacement of the theoretical framework.

C1.justification: V1 claims a first complete solution for exact volumetric Gaussian rendering. V2 narrows exactness to projective geometry and reframes the integral contribution as establishing the connection to an existing maximum-response heuristic. Its abstract and introduction also explicitly claim generalization to wider FoVs unseen during training. This substantially revises the scope and novelty of the central claims.

C2.justification: New Appendix A acknowledges ordering, overlap, self-attenuation, and occasional popping artifacts, explicitly disclaiming full physical volumetric exactness. V2 also adds substantive explanations of densification's limits, mismatched-culling artifacts, GOF instability, and why full-FoV perspective supervision can underperform central crops. These extend the original interpretation substantially.

D1.justification: V2 adds explicit CUDA numerical-stability implementation discussion, identifies H200 hardware for scaling experiments, and states that code/video/HTML accompany supplementary material, with training/evaluation scripts planned for release. Most initialization, hyperparameter, reprojection, and camera-pose details already existed in v1 and are relocated to Appendix G. The PDFs do not independently establish actual code availability.

R1.justification: V2 substantially repositions the contribution through Celarek et al.'s scaling argument, new comparisons with 2DGS and HTGS, and explicit recognition that its rendering expression matches prior maximum-response heuristics. Appendices A, D.3, and I expand comparisons of assumptions, exactness, and practical limitations. This goes beyond citation updates or EVER's publication-year change.

P1.justification: The introduction, related work, and method narrative are extensively rewritten. Preliminaries and the full rendering derivation move into Appendix B, ablations are integrated into Section 4, and implementation information is consolidated in Appendix G. A contents list and new limitations, ethics, reproducibility, and usage statements further reorganize the document.

P2.justification: The two-column ACM layout becomes a single-column ICLR layout. V1 Figures 3–4 are combined into v2 Figure 2, runtime tables and ScanNet++ visuals move to appendices, and the ZipNeRF qualitative display is redesigned. Expanded comparison tables and new scaling, extreme-FoV, stability, and Aria figures substantially change the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially improves scientific qualification and empirical support. Appendix A addresses v1's overly broad exact-volumetric framing, while new scaling, transmittance-replacement, stability, and unseen-FoV tests directly examine the claimed advantages. These gains extend beyond additional benchmark scores. Some blanket performance claims remain overstated: Table 4 still gives EVER higher SSIM than 3DGEER, 0.825 versus 0.821, despite the all-metrics wording.
